title: fix(plugin-auth)!: an SSO provider's domain list takes bare host names only, and every rule reads each entry the same way
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D58H4hn7mx9bRShF3BfEhTw)_

Fixes #32960
Fixes #32975

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — narrowed: `POST /sso/register`, `POST /sso/update-provider` and the bridges that re-dispatch to them answer `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on `domain` (`fields[0].code: 'invalid_value'`, naming the entry) for a `domain` value holding an entry that is not a bare host name, where they stored it; SCIM adoption of an existing SSO account no longer reads an entry or an address that only folds into a host (full-width letters) as a domain. Widened: SCIM adoption reads an entry and an address in their one spelling, so a root dot and the Unicode / punycode forms of an internationalised name name the same domain, as the account rule already read them. New module exports `ssoDomainEntryHost`, `ssoDomainEntryHosts`, `ssoDomainEntryNotBare` (`sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts`).
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no skill under `skills/**` teaches the SSO provider domain list; `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` gains the rule and the correction in this change.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：SSO 提供方的「域名列表」只收裸主机名（如 `acme.com`）。注册或修改时写成网址、带端口或路径（`https://acme.com`、`acme.com:443`）会被 400 拒绝并点名那一条，什么都不存。读这个列表的规则（新建账号的已证明域名规则、SCIM 接管已有账号）现在用同一个解析，同一条目在各规则下指同一个域名。
- 为什么改：#32669 之后，网址形状的条目会被存下、通过 DNS 验证，却在登录时什么都证明不了；SCIM 接管还用着另一套更松的解析。
- 风险与回滚：只拒绝新写入的非裸条目；已存的不改写。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts`（`ssoDomainEntryHost` / `ssoDomainEntryNotBare`），`scim-sso-adoption.ts`（改用共享解析），`auth-manager.ts` `assertSsoProviderDomainFree`（拒绝的接线）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/sso-account-at-proven-domain.test.ts src/sso-provider-lifecycle.test.ts`。
- 需要你做的：无，评审通过后区域线程落地。

## What changes

- **One parse** (`sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts`): `ssoDomainEntryHost(entry)` (the account rule's entry reading, now exported and named for what it is) and `ssoDomainEntryHosts(domain)` (the list). The account rule reads through them as before; `scim-sso-adoption.ts` drops its own split-trim-lowercase parse and reads the provider list through `ssoDomainEntryHosts` and the address through `ssoAddressDomain`. So an entry the parse does not accept (a URL, a port, a path) names no domain for SCIM either (#32975).
- **Register and edit refuse a non-bare entry** (#32960): `ssoDomainEntryNotBare(domain)` names the first entry the shared parse does not accept; `assertSsoProviderDomainFree` (the before-hook on `/sso/register` and a domain edit on `/sso/update-provider`, which the register bridges reach) throws it as `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on `domain`, after the length refusal and before the claim rule. Blank entries are skipped, as every parse of the list skips them. Nothing is saved.
- **The claim rule** (`sso-provider-lifecycle.ts` `providerDomains`, one provider per domain) is unchanged. With the refusal in front, every entry a request can now store reads the same under it as under the shared parse (pinned for every spelling in the table). A stored entry of ANOTHER provider saved before this rule (say `https://acme.com`) still blocks a collision on `acme.com`: the claim rule mirrors the vendor's address routing, which still reads it, so reading it more leniently there only ever refuses more.
- **Existing rows** are not rewritten; an edit that writes no domain is not judged. `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` says how to correct a stored entry (rewrite it as the bare host, then verify again).

## Why

#32960: with domain verification on, #32669 counts an entry as proven only when it is a bare host; a URL- or port-shaped entry was stored, passed the vendor's DNS check, and then admitted no one. #32975: three rules read the same list three ways; one stored entry could name a domain under one and not another.

## Verification

At head `a10e98535f` (branch point `origin/main` `e540baf8`; no file this PR touches changed on `main` since):

- `sso-account-at-proven-domain.test.ts` (+7): the account rule and the SCIM rule judged over 14 entry spellings × 5 addresses agree on every pair; non-bare entries name nothing for SCIM; SCIM reads a root dot and punycode as the same domain; CONTROL bare host under all three rules; every entry register accepts reads the same under the claim rule and the shared parse; the refusal names the entry with `VALIDATION_FAILED` / `invalid_value`; CONTROL bare names, blanks, empty.
- `sso-provider-lifecycle.test.ts` (+4): register (direct door and the SAML bridge) and a domain edit refuse five non-bare shapes with 400 naming the entry, nothing written, the stored domain kept; CONTROL bare names stored at register and edit; a provider stored with a URL entry before the rule is untouched by an edit without a domain and corrected by the documented edit. Two claim cases that used `https://…` request values now use `….` (a root dot) for the same "another spelling" leg, since the shape refusal answers a URL first.
- Targeted: `sso-account-at-proven-domain`, `sso-provider-lifecycle`, `scim-sso-adoption`: 87 passed.
- Ablations (fix committed, mutation, restore to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty): SCIM back to its own split-lowercase parse → 2 failed (the agreement table, the one-spelling case); the register refusal unwired in `assertSsoProviderDomainFree` → 2 failed (both door refusals).
- `@objectstack/plugin-auth` full suite: `Test Files 269 passed (269)`, `Tests 5125 passed | 10 skipped`; `typecheck` exit 0 (with `check:test-typecheck`).
- Gates: the derived families (`dispatch-gates --commands`) are read in the review request; CI runs the full set.
